dedupe_keys.name: usgs gfail lifelines gfroads probability of road and rail blockage from earthquake triggered landslides

description: gfail_lifelines is a USGS Python package, published on code.usgs.gov, for estimating impacts on lifelines from earthquake-triggered ground failure in near real time. Contents: its one module, gfroads, combines the areal coverage estimates of the USGS earthquake-triggered landslide model (Nowicki Jessee et al. 2017) with road data from Overture Maps or OpenStreetMap to estimate the probability that each road segment is affected; a rail option uses Overture rail data instead. Two command line programs are provided: run_gfroads, which takes a USGS event id and writes KMZ and GeoJSON files of blockage probabilities, and osmgfr, which pre-filters an OSM PBF file to the road classes gfroads uses. Producer: USGS (repository group ghsc/esi/groundfailure). Coverage: any earthquake with a USGS ground failure product; the README examples use the 2003 M6.3 Lefkada earthquake. Format and access: open source Python installed in a conda environment; a QGIS style file is included; Overture releases can be pinned by date. Licence: CC0 1.0 (repository licence). Caveats: probabilities inherit the uncertainty of the landslide model's areal coverage; OSM use was tested only on macOS Mojave and WSL. Simulation uses: rapid estimates of road and rail link closures after earthquakes to seed network connectivity, routing and emergency access analyses. Related records: data-overture-maps-transportation and data-usgs-shakemap-scenario-catalog.
